newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kurd rebels kills two in Turkish cafe attack.
newsitem.headline: Kurd rebels kills two in Turkish cafe attack.

text.p: Kurdish guerrillas have killed two people and wounded 17 in an attack on a cafe frequented by policemen in southeast Turkey, security officials said on Tuesday.
A group of around six Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels opened fire on the Ceylan cafe in the town of Maden on Monday night with a heavy machinegun and assault rifles.
The two dead were junior civil servants and six of the wounded were policemen, officials in the nearby town of Tunceli said.
More than 20,000 people have died in 12 years of conflict between government forces and the rebels, fighting for Kurdish self rule.
Security officials say a recent increase in PKK attacks south of Tunceli is probably due to the presence in the area of elusive rebel commander Semdin Sakik, also known as "Fingerless Zeki".
Sakik is believed to have entered Turkey from a hideout in northern Iraq in the last month.
